title: for Loops
goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how a for loop visits each item in a list and runs an indented block once per item.
learn: Write a for loop with for and in
Indent the lines that should repeat
Use the loop variable inside the block
idea: A for loop runs a block of code once for each item in a sequence, like a list. You write for name in names:. The name between for and in is the loop variable, and each time through the loop it holds the next item. Also indent the lines under the for line, because those indented lines are the block that repeats.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, add "Diana" to the names list so it has four names and press Run. You should see a fourth Hello line for Diana.

practice.text: Finish the loop so it prints each fruit on its own line.
practice.hint: Inside the loop, print the loop variable fruit. It holds apple, then banana, then cherry.
practice.starterTip: Replace print() with print(fruit) (keep the four spaces so it stays inside the for block).
practice.gradingNote: Pass if a for loop walks the fruits list and prints each fruit (or a line that includes each fruit).

practice.text: Loop over the colors list and print Color: then each color.
practice.hint: Use the loop variable color in print(). You can show a label and the value in one line.
practice.starterTip: Try print("Color:", color) on the indented line under for color in colors:.
practice.starter:
colors = ["red", "blue", "green"]
for color in colors:
    # Print Color: and the color
    print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if a for loop prints each color, preferably with the word Color.

quiz.question: How many times does this loop run? for name in ["A", "B", "C"]:
quiz.correct: Right, there are three items, so the loop body runs three times.
quiz.wrong: Count the items in the list. The loop runs once per item.

quiz.question: What is the loop variable in for color in colors:?
quiz.correct: Yes, color is the loop variable and it holds one item each time.
quiz.wrong: The name between for and in is the loop variable.

quiz.question: Why indent the lines under a for loop?

options.text: Indentation looks nicer but does nothing
Those lines are the block that repeats
Indentation makes the loop run faster
Only comments need to be indented

quiz.correct: Right, the indented lines belong to the loop and run every time through.
quiz.wrong: In Python, the indentation shows which lines are inside the loop.

project.title: Team Roster
project.desc: Loop through a list of three player names and print Player: then each name. After the loop, print Roster complete.
project.starter:
players = ["Maya", "Sam", "Leo"]
for player in players:
    print()

# After the loop
print()
